p: Rav Yosef, on the day of Atzeres,
said, "Prepare for me a choice third-grown calf."
אָמַר: אִי לָאו הַאי יוֹמָא דְּקָגָרַם,
He said, "Were it not for this day that brought it about,
how many a Yosef there are in the marketplace!"
together with the power of his Torah,
as against the rest of the unlearned;
and were it not for Matan Torah,
what would distinguish one man from other men?
"And it would be, as with the people, so with the Kohen" (Yeshayah 24:2).
there were many lofty and exalted souls
of far greater stature than the rest of the people,
such as the beis midrash of Shem and Ever
and the other great men of the generation.
Also, what is the meaning of the expression
עַל פִּי מֵימְרָא אַחֶרֶת דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
according to another statement of Rav Yosef
who said, "Do not teach 'humility' in the Mishnah,
For in truth Rav Yosef had
to the point that it did not enter his mind
that he had any advantage of his own,
רַק מִצַּד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
but only that he had a root in kedushah
from the aspect of being bound up
with the totality of the souls of Yisrael.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשֵׁם הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִבַּארְדִּיטְשׁוֹב,
And as they related in the name of the holy Rav of Berditchev,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the tzaddik be for a blessing in the life of the World to Come,
the berachah "Who has not made me a gentile";
and when they asked him about it,
he answered that upon rising from his bed
he felt great brokenness of heart,
and he had nothing with which
that at any rate his birth
stems from the root of the kedushah of Yisrael;
and he recited with great joy
the berachah "Who has not made me a gentile,"
and with this he restored his soul.
that from the moment of Matan Torah onward
the souls of Yisrael were set apart
from the souls of the nations of the world,
from a special treasury in kedushah.
וְכׇל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אֲחִיזָה בְּתוֹלָדָה
And whoever has a hold by birth
must necessarily be refined for the good
כְּאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה, א):
until all the souls in the Guf have been used up.
And to this Rav Yosef alludes:
"Were it not for this day that brought it about" —
the souls of Yisrael were set apart,
so that their root would be in kedushah by birth —
"how many a Yosef there are in the marketplace";
for it is known that the name Yosef
denotes the aspect of the tzaddik
And although he knew of himself
that he had not blemished the Bris,
וְאִם כֵּן עַל כׇּל פָּנִים הוּא צַדִּיק,
so that at any rate he was a tzaddik,
yet he, in his lowliness in his own eyes,
thought that this came not from his own striving
and his overcoming of the yetzer,
but only from his natural disposition from birth,
and that the yetzer had left him alone in this.
there are found a number such as these,
as is known from the story of the Baal Shem Tov
that all the deeds of the nations of the world
are reckoned as nothing and naught,
except for the souls of Yisrael,
stem from the root of kedushah,
